theme: Splitting data so no shard melts
title: Shard Assignment Under Skew, Cross-Shard Cost, and Resharding Stability
strategies: trivial: round-robin key placement assign[i]=i%K (the checker's own uniform-distributing reference construction)

greedy: LPT balanced bin-packing -- sort keys by weight descending, drop each into the currently least-loaded shard; minimizes size skew but ignores the transaction graph and the previous assignment entirely

strong: exploit that cost decomposes additively per key (quadratic imbalance term + per-edge cross-shard term + per-key migration term) -- initialize from the previous epoch's assignment (or, cold-start, by contracting the heaviest transaction edges first) then run deterministic single-key best-improvement local search on the exact 3-term objective, co-locating keys that transact together and accepting size imbalance when it pays off
invalid: wrong token count and out-of-range shard indices -> rejected before scoring
